definition: A loss damage waiver (LDW), also known as a collision damage waiver (CDW) or physical damage waiver (PDW), is a contractual agreement, typically used in vehicle or equipment rental transactions, under which the rental company agrees not to hold the renter financially liable for loss of or damage to the rented property. In vehicle rentals, an LDW functions as an optional protection plan. When the renter purchases the waiver, the rental company assumes the risk of loss or damage to the vehicle, subject to defined exclusions. Under Tex. Bus. & Com. Code § 92.156, exclusions may include losses resulting from unexplained disappearance or abandonment of the vehicle, damage intentionally caused by the renter, or damage arising from willful or wanton misconduct. In heavy equipment rentals, a similar arrangement is governed by Tex. Bus. & Com. Code §§ 93.002–93.007. A heavy equipment loss damage waiver releases the renter from certain liability for damage or loss of the rented equipment but, under § 93.007, the waiver is expressly not classified as insurance.
